title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the continuation of La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is working with a 'Teichmüller-type' group \underline{\mathfrak S}^+ attached to genus 1 (an extension related to SL(2,Z), with generators ρ, σ). The next page gives the presentation ρ^6=σ^4=1, ρ^3=σ^2, [σ,λ_∞]=1 with λ_∞=ρσρ^{-1}σρ. Here M is a rank-2 lattice (an abelian normal subgroup), and \underline M is a completion or enlargement of M carrying the induced action. The aim is to construct an endomorphism u of \underline{\mathfrak S}^+ that induces multiplication by an odd integer (or unit) μ=2ν+1 on the lattice part. It is the 'multiplication by μ' automorphism of the kind through which the cyclotomic character, or Ẑ^*, acts on the genus-1 Teichmüller tower.

On the previous page Grothendieck admits that his formal computations, done in a 'bigger' free group, are 'vaseux'. He proposes to make them rigorous with the intrinsic description (39): \underline{\mathfrak S}^+ = \mathfrak S^+_{S_0} ∧_{M_{S_0}} \underline M_{S_0}. This is the pushout (contracted product) of the extension 1→M→\mathfrak S^+→Q→1 along the equivariant map M→\underline M.

This page states the universal property of that pushout. A homomorphism \underline{\mathfrak S}^+→G into an S_0-group G is the same as a pair (40): u_{\underline M}: \underline M_{S_0}→G and u_{\mathfrak S}: \mathfrak S_{S_0}→G (equivalently \mathfrak S→G(S_0)). The pair must satisfy two conditions:
(a) the diagram (41) commutes, i.e. u_{\mathfrak S}|_M = u_{\underline M}∘(M→\underline M);
(b) (42) u_{\underline M} is equivariant, where \mathfrak S^+ acts on \underline M via its action on M and on G by conjugation through u_{\mathfrak S}.

In the case at hand G = \underline{\mathfrak S}^+, with:
- (43) u_{\underline M}(λ) = i(μ·λ), where i is the inclusion \underline M ↪ \mathfrak S^+;
- (44) u_{\mathfrak S} given by the explicit formulas (33): ρ↦ρ'=(correction)·ρ, σ↦σ'=y_0 ω^{1/2}σ, with corrections in M.

The remaining task is to check that (33) really defines a homomorphism \mathfrak S_{S_0}→G. The next page does this by verifying the relations of the presentation, reducing them to ρ'^3=σ'^2=ω and λ'_∞=μλ_∞.
errors: No mathematical error. The universal property stated is the standard one for a pushout of a group extension along an equivariant map of the abelian kernel.

Equivariance (b) for u_{\underline M}=μ·i is automatic once u_{\mathfrak S}(s) ≡ s modulo the abelian group \underline M, as is the case for the formulas (33). Multiplication by μ commutes with the linear action. The real content is therefore whether (33) respects the relations, which Grothendieck correctly identifies.
Minor notational slips: G versus G^+ superscripts in (40); \mathfrak S versus \mathfrak S^+ used interchangeably; the label (44) is reused on the next page.

ideas.what: Universal property of the pushout of a group extension along an equivariant homomorphism of the abelian kernel, used to define maps out of \underline{\mathfrak S}^+
ideas.modern_name: pushout extension / contracted product E ∧^M M'
ideas.where_published: contracted products appear throughout SGA (e.g. SGA 1, SGA 7) and the Longue Marche

ideas.what: Construction of an endomorphism of the genus-1 Teichmüller-type group inducing multiplication by an odd μ on the lattice, via explicit corrected images of the generators ρ, σ
ideas.modern_name: action of Ẑ^*/cyclotomic character on the profinite genus-1 Teichmüller group (cf. Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on \hat{SL_2(Z)}-type groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); later Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps for genus 1
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche (circulated notes) discusses such actions in genus 1

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a methodological step: it states the standard universal property of a pushout extension to make an explicit generator-level construction rigorous. Nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: In (40) the target is written G with a superscript (G^+ / G^*); the 'i.e.' clause reads '\mathfrak S → G(S_0)'.
Diagram (41) is drawn as a triangle: M_{S_0}→\mathfrak S^+_{S_0} on top, M_{S_0}→\underline M_{S_0} down, then u_{\underline M} and u_{\mathfrak S} both mapping to G. It is not a square.
In (43) a fraction-like symbol before i(μ·λ) is struck out.
In (44) the struck words 'défini par' sit over \mathfrak S^+_{S_0}; it reads u_{\mathfrak S}: \mathfrak S^+_{S_0}→G défini par (33).
In (42) the parenthetical reads '(via son action sur M_{S_0})' and '(via u_{\mathfrak S})'.
